_why: Which harness family can BUILD each discovered corpus family, or null. This is a CAPABILITY CLAIM and it is written down rather than inferred, because a mapping that lives in a .get() default is a mapping nobody can review or correct. null is a real and useful answer: it means editors do this and the pipeline cannot, which is the capability gap ranked by how many videos it appears in.
_checked: _assert_every_corpus_family_is_mapped fails the container at import if the index carries a family with no entry here. The first index built from the open-vocabulary pass returned {} from offered_treatments and marked all six families unmeasurable, because the names changed underneath a silent .get() and nothing said so.
_why_null: null means the pipeline has no family that BUILDS this. The caption families are null for a different reason and it is worth stating: running captions are the CAPTION LAYER, present on every job, not a per-beat text treatment — the corpus annotator was explicitly told to record them in caption_layer and keep them out of treatment. Their styling (per-word colour, kinetic build) is a caption-layer capability question, not a placement one.
_sfx_is_unobservable: NO discovered family maps to `sfx`, and that is an ABSENT, not a zero. The annotator is sent JPEG FRAMES and a transcript — it receives no audio at all, so it cannot observe a sound effect however many there are. Any sfx rate derived from this corpus is a measurement of what a deaf instrument saw. The old corpus reported sfx 0.82/25s from 14 beats; that number came from the same blind annotator.
_sfx: Only the two PURE sound families map to `sfx` — the family place_sfx builds. 'Icon/Logo Reveal with SFX' is a logo reveal that carries a sting: its sound is placeable but its character is visual, and counting it as sfx evidence would inflate the very number tier 1 is built on.
